heard: Astronomers once believed our single galaxy was the entire universe. Faint misty patches in space seemed to be simple gas clouds. Former high school Spanish teacher Edwin Hubble decided to inspect them. Using California's 100-inch Hooker telescope, he measured distant pulsing stars. Hubble proved Andromeda was a separate galaxy far outside our own. He then tracked light from far galaxies shifting toward red wavelengths. Farther galaxies receded faster, proving the universe is actively expanding. Albert Einstein visited Mount Wilson and called static space his biggest blunder. Until then, no one knew other galaxies even existed.
